title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 98
paragraphs: After this Datis sailed off with his army to make war first on Eretria, taking Ionians and Aeolians with him. After he had put to sea from Delos, the island trembled — for the first and last time, as the Delians told me, from before that day down to my own time. Surely the god had intended this as a portent to mankind of the evils that were to come. For in the time of Darius son of Hystaspes, of Xerxes son of Darius, and of Artaxerxes son of Xerxes — three generations in succession — more evils befell Greece than in the twenty generations before Darius, some inflicted on her by the Persians, others by her own leaders warring against one another for supremacy. It was thus no unreasonable thing that Delos, previously unshaken, should be shaken. And an oracle had been given about it that ran:
“Delos, too, will I move, unmoved though it has been before.”

In the Greek tongue these names have the following meanings: Darius means “Compeller,” Xerxes “Warrior,” Artaxerxes “Great Warrior.” So indeed the Greeks might rightly call these kings in their own language.
